supporting: the separation of cascade from selector matching and specificity

claims.claim: The CSS cascade is the algorithm used to combine property values when declarations from more than one source apply to an element.
Before a declaration can compete in the cascade, it must be relevant: its condition must match and its selector must match the element.

Origin and importance are considered before specificity and order of appearance; normal author declarations outrank normal user-agent declarations, while important declarations reverse the origin precedence.

Within an origin, normal declarations in a layer have lower priority than normal declarations outside layers; important declarations reverse layer order and take precedence over important declarations outside layers.
When competing declarations remain tied after the earlier cascade steps, order of appearance is used and the last declaration in document order wins.
Specificity is a later tie-breaker, so a declaration with lower specificity can win when it has higher origin, importance, or layer precedence.
